answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake and accumulate verifiable work history before it can transact at scale. Like a garden where a trellis only supports vines that have actually grown along it, reputation here is earned through completed, attested tasks rather than claimed at signup. Creating thousands of fake identities then becomes expensive: each one needs its own stake and its own costly history, while a single proven agent — rare and valuable as saffron — can be trusted more cheaply than a crowd of unproven newcomers.
